children: Sutanuka Ghosal Kolkata: Shares of Kalyan Jewellers, PC Jeweller and other jewellery firms on Wednesday fell by up to 4% as the Bureau of Indian Standard (BIS) raised gold hallmarking fee from 45 to 75 per article with immediate effect.

Shares of newly listed Lalithaa Jewellery Mart also hit 5% lower circuit. Hallmarking charge has been increased from 45 to 75 per article, irrespective of its weight. This means a 1 gram piece and a substantially heavier jewellery article attract the same 75 compliance charge, making the increase far more significant in percentage terms for mass-market and middle-income consumers buying lightweight jewellery.

A nearly 67% hike in mandatory jewellery hallmarking charges could disproportionately raise the cost of lightweight and lower-value gold jewellery, prompting the All-India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) to seek a review of the revised fee structure by BIS. However, hallmarking charge for silver has been retained at 35. The increase has been notified through the BIS (Hallmarking) Amendment Regulations, 2026, dated September 14, 2026.

With gold prices already at elevated levels, industry fears that higher fixed compliance cost could eventually be passed through the jewellery value chain, adding to the cost of every article. GJC chairman Rajesh Rokde said industry supports mandatory hallmarking but questioned the rationale for raising the per-article charge sharply at a time when hallmarking volumes have expanded significantly. "GJC and jewellery industry have consistently supported hallmarking because purity assurance and consumer confidence are fundamental to our trade. But support for hallmarking does not mean that a nearly 67% increase in the cost of mandatory compliance should pass without examination," Rokde said. "Hallmarking volumes have expanded enormously. The industry, therefore, deserves to understand why the per-article charge needs to rise from 45 to 75 at this stage," he added.

title: Gold Hallmarking Fee Raised by Nearly 67%
